correctness.rationale: On each strict sorting chamber the map is a permutation. Splitting a generic segment at coordinate crossings and using the triangle inequality gives the upper maximum over permutation norms; continuity handles segments lying in ties. A small arbitrary perturbation inside each chamber gives the reverse inequality. On the mean-zero subspace, the nearest-neighbor path Laplacian with degree-one ends has eigenmodes cos((j-1/2)k pi/N) by the second-difference equation (with equal ghost and endpoint values). The extreme nonzero eigenvalues are 4 sin^2(theta) and 4 cos^2(theta), theta=pi/(2N). Their eigenspaces are simple. For even N, reflection pairs opposite signs in both modes and sine/cosine complementation matches magnitudes, so a permutation attains the spectral ratio. For odd N the lowest mode has a zero coordinate while the highest has none; compactness and the finite permutation family make the inequality strict. For the odd lower bound, write v_(h+l)=(-1)^(h+l-1) cos(l pi/N), h=(N+1)/2. In increasing rank, expressing v as -cos of angles yields the even-angle grid when N=3 mod 4 (0 once and other angles twice) and the odd-angle grid when N=1 mod 4 (pi once and others twice). This matches the low-mode midpoints within theta in every rank. The positive semidefinite defect lambda_max I-L annihilates v, so the energy deficit of the permuted low mode is at most lambda_max N theta^2, giving the stated odd lower bound and asymptotic. Each sorted-value gap is crossed by at least one original path edge, whose square dominates the sum of its crossed gap squares, proving the separate one-point bound. A different-coordinate SVD enumeration (python /workspace/independent_checks.py 2) checked 872 permutations over N=2–6; this is finite numerical corroboration only.
